newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia awards shipbuilding contract to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia awards shipbuilding contract to Japan.

text.p: Malaysian Bulk Carriers Sdn Bhd (MBC) on Wednesday awarded contracts to Sumitomo Corp and Onomichi Dockyard Co Ltd of Japan to build two 46,500 deadweight tonne product tankers for delivery in 1998.
MBC chairman Teo Joo Kim said the company has now contracted for four 46,500 dwt product tankers from Japanese shipyards, two of them to be delivered this year.
The four tankers cost more than 300 million ringgit, he said.

MBC is joint venture between Pacific Carriers Ltd of Singapore which holds a 49 percent stake, Malayan Sugar Manufacturing Company Bhd with 20 percent and Global Maritime Ventures Bhd with 31 percent.
MBC's current fleet of 19 vessels, totalling 488,000 dwt, consisted mainly of dry bulk carriers and a chemical tanker, Teo said.
The shipper, mainly a dry-goods bulk carrier now, wants to become a medium-range product tanker operator, starting with the four on order, Teo said.
